title: The degree-diameter problem: large graphs of given maximum degree and diameter
keeper: F. Comellas, The (Degree, Diameter) Problem for Graphs (web.mat.upc.edu/francesc.comellas/delta-d)
revision: table_degree_diameter.html read 15 Nov 2026 11:03 UTC (SHA-256 in page_sha256)

template.title: Degree-diameter problem ({delta},{d}): a large graph of maximum degree {delta} and diameter {d}
template.statement: Find a graph with maximum degree at most {delta} and diameter at most {d}, with as many vertices as possible.
template.submission: Text file: one graph in graph6 or sparse6, or an edge list, one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0; see checkers/degdiam_check.py.

score: the number of vertices (larger is better)
best_text: The largest known graph in Comellas's table has {best} vertices ({holder}); a graph with more vertices improves it.
bound_source: the Moore bound 1 + delta (sum of (delta-1)^i, i < d), not reached (not a cell field)
holder_unknown: named on the entry's page in the table
holder_sources: each entry's page (desc_g/...) names the graph and its authors
open_rule: every entry of the table (degree 3 to 16, diameter 2 to 10) not in boldface, with at most 20,000 vertices
left_out: 7 optimal (bold), 62 more than 20,000 vertices, 20 single problems
